source: FindMyPast — British Army Lists & Commission Registers 1661-1826; British Army Officer Promotions 1800-1815 (© Chris Daniell), each citing the London Gazette; Kent Burials (Medway Archives); Kentish Gazette and Kentish Weekly Post via FindMyPast newspapers
lede: This archive has carried Robert D'Arcy's career on the authority of Connolly's Roll of Officers of the Corps of Royal Engineers — a book printed in 1898. Every step of it can now be cited to the London Gazette instead, with issue and page, and it begins two years earlier than anything else here.

career.note: His first commission, and now the earliest record of him anywhere in this archive — a year before he married at Portsea and two before his son was christened there.

career.src: St Michael, Barbados — christenings of CONSTANTINE (18 Feb 1786) and JANE (17 Mar 1788), father Robert, mother Jane
career.note: NOT A COMMISSION — a posting, inferred from two christenings this archive already held and had never set against this chronology. Between the commission of 1778 and the majority of 1802 this career is a blank of twenty-four years. These are the only two records that fall inside it, and they put him in the West Indies with his wife in the middle of the 1780s.

The SAME Ordnance Office announcement, printed on the SAME page of the Gazette and in the same column of the Limerick Gazette, the Kentish Gazette and the Kentish Weekly Post, promoted his son CONSTANTINE D'ARCY to first lieutenant of the same corps. The archive found this page in July and read the father's line without noticing the son's.

career.became: Colonel in the Army by Brevet
career.src: War Office, 7 June 1813 — by the Prince Regent

career.note: Found in the Gazette itself before the subscription was opened.

career.unit: late of the Corps of Royal Engineers
career.note: Died at Chatham and was interred there with military honours on the 19th.

span: Forty-nine years from a practitioner engineer's commission to a major-general's grave.

joseph.head: And his son went to the guns, not the sappers.
joseph.body: Joseph D'Arcy — baptised at Portsea in March 1780, son of Robert and Jean — appears in FindMyPast's British Army, Royal Artillery Officers 1716-1899 from 1795, in the Army List of 1798, in the Commission Registers in 1802, 1803 and 1826, among the officer promotions of 1803, 1804 and 1806, and in the Army Lists of 1840, 1841, 1843 and 1844.
joseph.means: Commissioned at about fifteen and still listed at sixty-four. The Royal Artillery, not his father's Corps of Engineers. The detail of those entries is behind a further paywall even on a trial — the index is visible and the transcripts are not — so this is a career sketched from a list of dates rather than read.

notHim: One entry was discarded. A Robert D'Arcy is gazetted CORNET BY PURCHASE in the 17th Regiment of Light Dragoons on 19 May 1804, described as “Gent”, vice Harris. That is a young man buying his first commission in a cavalry regiment in 1804 — while this Robert D'Arcy had been a major since 1802 and was a lieutenant-colonel by the following March. Same name, different man, and the sort of thing that quietly wrecks a career chronology if nobody looks at the rank.

post.head: And a post, not just a rank.
post.body: The Kentish Gazette of 14 May 1805, reporting the death of his son, calls him “COL. D'ARCY, CHIEF ENGINEER OF CHATHAM LINES”. The Chatham Lines were the bastioned fortifications thrown up to defend the dockyard and the Medway — the largest engineering work in Kent. Every other record of Robert D'Arcy gives a rank. This one gives him a job.
